items.title: Section: Establishment Through Arising — A Single Causal Chain From Relinquishing Wealth to Realising Suchness

items.zh: 云何如是波羅蜜多，由生起故，次第建立？謂諸菩薩，先於財位無所顧戀，棄家諸欲，受淨尸羅。敬重戒故，能忍他惱，不惱於他。受持淨戒修習忍已，戒淨無動，無間無斷，於諸善品勤修加行。如是修習勤精進故，離諸放逸，能觸妙善心一境性。心得定故，如實了知，觀見一切所知境界。當知是名由生起故，次第建立。
items.en:
Second, through arising; first, posing the question. Why, through arising, are they established in this sequence?
Second, explaining. Bodhisattvas, first, harbouring no attachment to wealth or position, relinquish every household desire and receive pure moral discipline. Revering this discipline, one is able to bear with others' own vexation, never vexing them in turn. Having received pure discipline and cultivated patience, discipline itself becomes pure and unshakable, continuous without interruption, and one diligently applies effort towards every wholesome quality. Through this diligent cultivation, one departs from every laxity, and is able to touch excellent, wholesome one-pointedness of mind. Because the mind has attained concentration, one genuinely knows exactly as it is, observing and beholding every object of knowledge.
Third, the conclusion. One should understand this is what is meant by establishment through arising.

items.title: Section: Establishment Through Ripening-Fruit Begins — Generosity's Own External Result, Abundant Wealth in the World to Come

items.zh: 云何如是波羅蜜多，由異熟果，次第建立？謂諸菩薩於現法中，精勤修學施等善法；由是因緣，於當來世獲得種種外妙珍財無不圓滿，當知是施波羅蜜多因力所作。
items.en:
Third, through ripening-fruit; first, posing the question. Why, through ripening-fruit, are they established in this sequence?
Second, explaining; first, external circumstances brought to fulfilment. Bodhisattvas, in the present life, diligently cultivate generosity and the other wholesome dharmas; by this cause and condition, in the world to come, they obtain every kind of excellent, external, precious wealth, entirely without deficiency. One should understand this is the result of the perfection of generosity's own causal power.

items.title: Section: Three Internal Fruits — Long Life From Discipline, Innate Patience, and Innate Courage

items.zh: 獲得內五自體圓滿，是餘戒等波羅蜜多因力所作。云何內五自體圓滿？謂善趣攝若天若人，於餘有情壽等殊勝，當知是名第一圓滿。若有俱生於善加行常無厭倦，堪忍他惱，不樂惱他，當知是名第二圓滿。若有俱生普於一切所作事業堅固勇猛，當知是名第三圓滿。
items.en:
Second, internal circumstances brought to fulfilment; first, naming it. Obtaining the five kinds of internal, personal fulfilment is the result of the remaining perfections' own causal power.
Second, posing the question. What are these five kinds of internal, personal fulfilment?
Third, explaining; first, excellence of lifespan. Whether reborn among the gods or humans, within the fortunate realms, surpassing other sentient beings in lifespan and the like — one should understand this as the first fulfilment.
Second, an innate capacity to endure. Possessing, from birth, an untiring constancy in wholesome effort, able to bear others' own vexation, never wishing to vex them in return — one should understand this as the second fulfilment.
Third, an innate correspondence with courage. Possessing, from birth, firm, courageous resolve towards every undertaking — one should understand this as the third fulfilment.

items.title: Section: Innately Thin Affliction, and Innately Sharp Intelligence — Closing All Three Causes for the Sequence

items.zh: 若有俱生性薄塵穢，於其自心能自在轉，心有堪能於一切義速證通慧，當知是名第四圓滿。若有俱生於一切義其慧廣大聰敏捷利，當知是名第五圓滿。應知是名由異熟果，如是六種波羅蜜多次第建立。
items.en:
Fourth, an innate thinness of affliction. Possessing, from birth, a nature only lightly touched by worldly dust and defilement, sovereign over one's own mind, capable of swiftly realising penetrating wisdom regarding any matter — one should understand this as the fourth fulfilment.
Fifth, an innate possession of sharp intelligence. Possessing, from birth, vast, sharp, quick-witted wisdom regarding every matter — one should understand this as the fifth fulfilment.
Third, the conclusion. One should understand it is through ripening-fruit that these six perfections are established in this sequence.

items.title: Section: Why Exactly Six — Four Perfections Serving Discipline, and Nothing Beyond the Three Trainings

items.zh: 由前四種波羅蜜多資糧、自性、眷屬、守護，當知圓滿修諸菩薩增上戒學；由其靜慮波羅蜜多，當知圓滿修諸菩薩增上心學；由其般若波羅蜜多，當知圓滿修諸菩薩增上慧學。過此三上，更無菩薩學道可得，是故此三普攝一切菩薩學道。由此建立波羅蜜多唯有六種。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
Second, exactly six in number; first, mapping them individually onto the three trainings. Through the first four perfections — provisions, intrinsic nature, supporting companion, and guardian — one should understand that a bodhisattva's own heightened training in discipline is brought to fulfilment.
Commentary: Regarding "provisions, intrinsic nature, supporting companion, and guardian" — the perfection of generosity is discipline's own provisions; the perfection of discipline is discipline's own intrinsic nature; the perfection of patience is discipline's own supporting companion; the perfection of diligence is discipline's own guardian. One should understand that the training in discipline is brought to fulfilment through exactly this sequence.
Through the perfection of meditative absorption, one should understand that a bodhisattva's own heightened training in mind is brought to fulfilment. Through the perfection of wisdom, one should understand that a bodhisattva's own heightened training in wisdom is brought to fulfilment.
Second, concluding that nothing lies beyond or can be added. Beyond these three, no further bodhisattva path of learning can be found; these three thereby comprehensively gather in the entirety of the bodhisattva's own path of learning. By this, the perfections are established as exactly six in number — nothing beyond this number, and nothing to be added to it.

items.title: Section: Four Things a Bodhisattva Should Always Undertake — Gathering In Everything Still to Be Done

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略有四種所應作事，由是普攝一切所作。何等為四？
items.en:
Second, clarifying the four things always to be undertaken; first, naming them. Bodhisattvas, in brief, have four things they should always undertake, by which every one of their own undertakings is comprehensively gathered in.
Second, posing the question. What are the four?

items.title: Section: Four Things Always to Be Done, Mapped Onto the Four Kinds of Conduct — Closing the Entire Chapter on Conduct

items.zh: 一者、為證菩提修諸善行；二者、由此為先達真實義；三者、圓證威力；四者、成熟有情。如是四種菩薩所作，當知是先所說四行，如其次第所為所立。是故過此，更不建立有諸餘行。
items.en:
Third, listing them. First, cultivating every wholesome practice for the sake of realising awakening. Second, with this as the forerunner, penetrating genuine, ultimate reality. Third, fully realising majestic spiritual power. Fourth, maturing sentient beings.
Fourth, mapping them. These four bodhisattva undertakings, one should understand, are exactly the four kinds of conduct already explained, established in this same sequence for this same purpose. This is why, beyond these four, no further conduct needs to be established.
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the third yoga foundation of ultimate practice, the chapter on establishment, part five, part one.

items.title: Section: One Hundred Forty Exclusive Buddha-Qualities Named — the Thirty-Two Marks Begin

items.zh: 依如來住及依如來到究竟地，諸佛世尊有百四十不共佛法。謂諸如來三十二大丈夫相、八十隨好、四一切種清淨、十力、四無所畏、三念住、三不護、大悲、無忘失法、永害習氣，及一切種妙智。云何如來三十二種大丈夫相？
items.en:
Third, gathered within the later chapter on establishment; first, naming the scope. Relying on the abode of the Tathāgata, and relying on the Tathāgata's own ground of ultimate accomplishment, the buddhas, the world-honoured ones, possess a hundred and forty exclusive buddha-dharmas.
Second, listing them. The thirty-two marks of a great being, the eighty exemplary signs, the four kinds of complete purity of every sort, the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three foundations of mindfulness, the three things requiring no guarding, great compassion, the dharma of never forgetting, the permanent destruction of habitual tendencies, and wondrous wisdom of every kind.
Third, explaining; first, displaying each individually; first, the marks and exemplary signs together; first, gathered as resultant fruit; first, listing the marks and signs; first, the thirty-two marks; first, posing the question. What are the Tathāgata's own thirty-two marks of a great being?

items.title: Section: Marks One Through Eight — Level-Soled Feet, Wheel-Marked Soles, Webbed Fingers, and Legs Like a Deer-King

items.zh: 一者、具大丈夫足善安住等案地相，是大丈夫大丈夫相。二者、於雙足下現千輻輪，轂輞眾相無不圓滿。三者、具大丈夫纖長指相。四者、足跟趺長。五者、手足細軟。六者、手足網縵。七者、立手摩膝。八者、瑿泥耶踹。
items.en: Second, listing them. First, possessing the great being's own feet, resting evenly, firmly planted upon the ground — this is the great being's own mark among great beings. Second, beneath both soles appear thousand-spoked wheels, every hub, rim, and mark entirely complete. Third, possessing the great being's own slender, long fingers. Fourth, a full, rounded instep. Fifth, soft, supple hands and feet. Sixth, webbed hands and feet. Seventh, standing, the hands reach past the knees. Eighth, calves like the deer-king's own.

items.title: Section: Marks Nine Through Sixteen — An Upright Body, Concealed Modesty, and Skin of Golden Radiance

items.zh: 九者、身不僂曲。十者、勢峯藏密。十一者、身相圓滿如諾瞿陀。十二者、常光一尋。十三者、身毛上靡。十四者、身諸毛孔一一毛生，如紺青色螺文右旋。十五者、身皮金色。十六者、身皮細滑，塵垢不著。
items.en: Ninth, a body that never stoops, broad and upright. Tenth, male organs concealed within the body like a horse's own. Eleventh, a body perfectly proportioned like a banyan tree. Twelfth, a constant radiance extending one fathom. Thirteenth, every bodily hair curling upwards. Fourteenth, each pore producing a single hair, deep blue-black, spiraling to the right. Fifteenth, skin of true golden colour. Sixteenth, skin fine and smooth, untouched by dust or defilement.

items.title: Section: Marks Seventeen Through Twenty-Four — Seven Full Places, a Lion's Own Upper Body, and Forty Even Teeth

items.zh: 十七者、於其身上兩手、兩足、兩肩及項七處皆滿。十八者、其身上半如師子王。十九者、肩善圓滿。二十者、髆間充實。二十一者、身分洪直。二十二者、具四十齒，皆悉齊平。二十三者、其齒無隙。二十四者、其齒鮮白。
items.en: Seventeenth, seven places full of flesh: both hands, both feet, both shoulders, and the neck. Eighteenth, an upper body like a lion-king's own. Nineteenth, perfectly rounded shoulders. Twentieth, full flesh between the shoulders. Twenty-first, a body upright and proportioned. Twenty-second, forty perfectly even teeth. Twenty-third, teeth without any gap. Twenty-fourth, teeth brilliantly white.

blocks.text: The chapter on conduct ends, and the chapter on establishment begins: the hundred and forty qualities unique to a buddha, starting with the thirty-two marks of a great person.
Venerable Miào Jìng: knowing as it is comes through study of sūtras, vinaya, and treatises. Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on one-pointed absorption, one knows things as they are.
"Obtaining every external precious wealth is the result of the perfection of giving." Master Cháng Bǎi: wealth now comes from giving in past lives.
Venerable Miào Jìng: inborn, not taught: what you delighted in doing in a past life, you delight in now.
Venerable Miào Jìng: defilement is thin, not absent but slight; such a person sits and easily gains concentration.

Provisions, nature, companion, and guardian of the training in discipline; beyond the three trainings there is nothing further. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving is the provision for keeping precepts; diligence guards them.

"First, cultivating wholesome practice for awakening; second, preceded by this, penetrating true reality; third, realising power; fourth, maturing beings." Venerable Miào Jìng: skipping wholesome practice and going straight to the ultimate lacks proper sequence.

The thirty-two marks, eighty signs, four kinds of purity, ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and more. Master Cháng Bǎi: none is shared with the two vehicles or outsiders. Venerable Miào Jìng: a mark adorns a major part of the body; the eighty signs adorn the marks.
Venerable Miào Jìng: when the foot touches the ground it is even. Master Cháng Bǎi: the sole is flat and soft with no hollow. On long arms, Venerable Miào Jìng: the hand can touch the knee.
The thirty-two marks can seem strange to a modern reader. Tomorrow's passage explains why the Buddha taught them at all: each mark points back to a practice.

quiz.q: In the arising sequence, "with the mind concentrated, one knows as it is." The English note credits concentration alone. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: knowing as it is requires training in sūtra, vinaya, and treatise; Cháng Bǎi: relying on one-pointed absorption, one knows as it is
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: knowing as it is comes through study of the sūtras, vinaya, and treatises. Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on one-pointed absorption, one knows things as they are.

quiz.q: External precious wealth comes from the causal power of which perfection?
quiz.why: "Obtaining every external precious wealth is the result of the perfection of giving." Master Cháng Bǎi: wealth now comes from giving in past lives.

quiz.q: The inner fulfillments often say "俱生." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: inborn, not taught — what one loved doing in the last life one loves in this
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: inborn, not taught by anyone; what you delighted in doing in a past life you delight in now. Master Cháng Bǎi: practising patience makes the inborn capacity to endure especially strong.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "innately thin afflictions"?
options: defilement is thin — not absent, but slight; such people easily attain concentration, cultivated in past lives
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: defilement is thin — not absent, but slight; such a person sits and easily gains concentration — the fruit of past cultivation. Master Cháng Bǎi: not easily drawn to the six objects.

quiz.q: How do the first four fulfil the training in discipline, and why exactly six?
options: giving as provisions, discipline as nature, patience as companion, diligence as guardian; nothing beyond the three trainings, hence six
quiz.why: Provisions, nature, companion, guardian of the training in discipline; beyond the three trainings there is nothing further, so exactly six. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving is the provision for keeping precepts; diligence guards them.

quiz.q: What is the first of the bodhisattva's four undertakings?
quiz.why: "First, cultivating wholesome practice for awakening; second, preceded by this, penetrating true reality; third, realising power; fourth, maturing beings." Master Cháng Bǎi: broadly the six or ten perfections, briefly the three trainings.

quiz.q: "Preceded by this, penetrating true reality." The English says "taking this as foremost." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: first cultivate good, then penetrate — going straight to the ultimate without good practice lacks proper order
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: skipping wholesome practice and going straight to the ultimate lacks proper sequence. "By this first" means preceded by it; the English "foremost" misses this.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate these four undertakings to the four kinds of conduct?
options: same sequence as the four kinds of conduct
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the same order as the four kinds of bodhisattva conduct. Master Cháng Bǎi: these four include every bodhisattva undertaking.

quiz.q: What do the hundred and forty exclusive buddha-qualities include?
options: thirty-two marks, eighty signs, four purities, ten powers, four fearlessnesses, three mindfulnesses, three unguardeds, great compassion, unforgetfulness, habits destroyed, wisdom of all aspects
quiz.why: Thirty-two marks, eighty signs, four kinds of purity, ten powers, four fearlessnesses, three mindfulnesses, three unguarded, great compassion, unforgetfulness, destruction of habits, and wisdom of all aspects. Master Cháng Bǎi: not shared with the two vehicles or outsiders.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish marks and exemplary signs?
options: marks adorn major parts; the eighty signs adorn the marks
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a mark is an adornment of a major part; the eighty signs adorn the marks.

quiz.q: The first mark — feet resting evenly on the ground. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: the foot meets the ground evenly; Cháng Bǎi: the sole is flat and soft, no hollow, stepping steadily
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: when the foot touches the ground it is even. Master Cháng Bǎi: the sole is flat and soft with no hollow, stepping steadily.

quiz.q: Mark seven is rendered "reach past the knees"; mark four "instep." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read them?
options: the hand reaches the knee — long arms; the heel extends backward
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the hand can touch the knee — long arms; the heel seems to extend backward. The English "past the knees" and "instep" differ from this.
